description: How one CVE is fixed, as its sources state it, in one answer. Every text is relayed as stated by its source; EchelonGraph has not tested it. An empty list or a remediation_state of none_in_source or not_parsed is not a finding that no fix exists. Returns fix_status (the API's fix-status rule: state and basis), cisa (for a KEV-listed CVE CISA's required_action, due_date, short_description and notes_urls, verbatim; CISA's required_action is directed at US federal civilian agencies (under BOD 26-04, which replaced BOD 22-01 on 10 June 2026) and is not EchelonGraph's advice.), fixed_branches (each affected package with fixed_branches: every affected range, introduced and fixed or last_affected, and fixed_version, one range's fix), vendor_remediations (each vendor advisory naming the CVE, with remediation_state, remediation_kinds and items, each with kind, source_category, text and url), fix_references (references NVD or the CNA tagged Patch or Mitigation), patches, coverage and failed_sections. kind is the vendor's own category (vendor_fix, workaround, mitigation, no_fix_planned, none_available or other), or may be no_fix_planned if Cisco's summary says none will be released. remediation_state is parsed, none_in_source (none listed for this CVE), not_parsed (that vendor's remediation is not read) or withdrawn. ecosystem, package and version (all three or none, sent in request headers, never in the URL) add installed, the verdict at that version, and fixed_in, the lowest unaffected version above it, or null with fixed_in_reason. A section the API could not read is named in failed_sections, not relayed as empty. A REJECTED CVE answers not_assessed. Past 30,000 characters of JSON, the first text block holds data cut to fit, and the note says what the cut leaves out and where to read it (TEXT CUT); so is structured data (DATA CUT), unless full: true. Cut, vendor texts are shortened first; kinds, states and URLs are kept.

ecosystem.description: Installed version, with package and version: the package's ecosystem, such as npm, PyPI or Maven. Sent in a request header.

full.description: true: data in the structured result is the answer whole, however long. Without it, a structured result past 30,000 characters of JSON has its data cut (DATA CUT): in an order the note states, the entries of its longest lists keep only some of their fields, and then the lists only some of their entries; data_truncated is true, and truncated gives each list cut with its total, the number returned and whether its entries are thinned. Whole data is for a program; a client that sizes structured results, as Claude Code does against MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS, can refuse an answer past its cap.

package.description: Installed version, with ecosystem and version: the package name in that ecosystem, such as org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core. Sent in a request header.

version.description: Installed version, with ecosystem and package: the version installed, such as 2.14.1. Sent in a request header.

name: cve_remediation

installed_asked.description: The installed version this call sent (in request headers), as given; null when none.

parsed_vendors.description: The vendors whose remediation EchelonGraph parses.

sections_failed.description: The sections the API could not read (its failed_sections); null when the answer does not say.

vendors_not_parsed.description: The vendors in this answer whose remediation EchelonGraph does not parse.

coverage.description: What the answer covers; null where the answer says nothing about it.

required_action.description: CISA's requiredAction, verbatim. CISA's required_action is directed at US federal civilian agencies (under BOD 26-04, which replaced BOD 22-01 on 10 June 2026) and is not EchelonGraph's advice.

fix_status.description: The API's fix-status rule for the CVE, the one CVE Pulse pages show: state is available (a fix is on record), fix_referenced (a reference tagged Patch, often a source commit, and no release confirmed), fix_merged (an upstream fix merged, not yet in a tagged release), none_confirmed (no fix evidence on record, which is not a finding that no fix exists) or unknown (an input could not be read). basis is the step of the rule that decided it; described_by is the CVE description's sentence naming the fix, solution_by the CVE record's solution sentence naming it (statement) and the CNA that wrote it (cna), stated_in_record that patch_evidence counts a fix the CVE record states with no sentence to quote, listed_in_patch_table that a fixed version or patch row is on record; unread_inputs names any input the API could not read. vendor_released (basis vendor_fix_released) is the vendor's own statement that a fix is released where the CVE record names no fixed version: its sentence, verbatim (statement, or null), never a version, so the fixed release is the vendor advisory's to name. solution_by's section is workarounds when the fix sentence is the record's workaround, not its solution.

last_affected.description: The range's last affected version, where no fix is on record; never a fix.

fixed_branches_truncated.description: Present only where the structured result's cut (DATA CUT) kept this package's first ranges, not all: total, its ranges in the answer; returned, the ones data keeps. The same call with full: true returns every range.

fixed_version.description: One range's fix, kept for compatibility; not the fix for every affected range.

fixed_in.description: With an installed version: the first version above it that no affected range on record holds, always above it, as the advisory states it, or, where installed.version_evidence is cna_affected_range, the CVE record's CNA range: the fixed bound of the range holding it, moved past any overlapping range that still holds that bound (fixed_in_detail then names it). null when no range on record holds it, no fix is on record past the ranges holding it, or the version was not assessed, with fixed_in_reason saying which. Absent when no installed version was asked. Where fixed_in_dispute is set, the CVE record's CNA and the advisory disagree on the range that holds the version, and fixed_in follows the source its higher names (its note says how), not the advisory alone.

fixed_in_detail.description: Set when fixed_in is not the fixed bound of the range holding the installed version: the overlapping ranges of the same record it moved past, which still hold that bound.

fixed_in_dispute.description: Once EchelonGraph's API serves it, set where the API found the CVE record's CNA and the advisory disagreeing on the range that holds this version. kind: fixed (they disagree on where the package is fixed) or introduced (the CNA's range starts below where the advisory's does). The advisory's bound in dispute, exactly one of advisory_fixed, advisory_last_affected and advisory_introduced, as the advisory's own statement gives it (advisory_listed: it lists affected versions rather than a range, and the bound is a version it lists), and advisory_id, the advisory. cna (name, short_name), cna_product (what the CNA's entry names, as the API reads it) and cna_range (version, less_than or less_than_or_equal, status, version_type; changes, each {at, status}, where the range's status changes inside it, with changes_truncated where the record held more): the CNA's range in dispute, as the API reads the record (where higher is cna, the CNA's range that reaches past the advisory's bound: on a cna_affected_range match it holds the version, and on an advisory_interval or exact_version_list match it holds the advisory's bound past the version (its fix, or the versions just above its last affected or listed version), so it may start above the version; where higher is advisory, the CNA's range that ends below it, the CNA saying the version is fixed), from an entry the record writes, or, with cna_range_default true, a span no entry writes that the record's defaultStatus covers. higher: the source the answer follows, the more conservative one (cna or advisory). note: the API's sentence on the dispute and what the answer does with it, relayed verbatim. Fields and values a later API adds are relayed. Its absence is not a finding that the CNA agrees: an API that does not serve it yet, or older than the field, sends none; one that serves it reads a CNA's ranges only where it applies them and only from an entry it matches to the package; and a match the CNA's range alone raises may carry none.

fixed_in_reason.description: Why fixed_in is null; absent when fixed_in is a version.

ecosystem.description: The ecosystem asked for, in its canonical OSV spelling.

fixed_in_dispute.description: Once EchelonGraph's API serves it, set where the API found the CVE record's CNA and the advisory disagreeing on the range that holds this version. kind: fixed (they disagree on where the package is fixed) or introduced (the CNA's range starts below where the advisory's does). The advisory's bound in dispute, exactly one of advisory_fixed, advisory_last_affected and advisory_introduced, as the advisory's own statement gives it (advisory_listed: it lists affected versions rather than a range, and the bound is a version it lists), and advisory_id, the advisory. cna (name, short_name), cna_product (what the CNA's entry names, as the API reads it) and cna_range (version, less_than or less_than_or_equal, status, version_type; changes, each {at, status}, where the range's status changes inside it, with changes_truncated where the record held more): the CNA's range in dispute, as the API reads the record (where higher is cna, the CNA's range that reaches past the advisory's bound: on a cna_affected_range match it holds the version, and on an advisory_interval or exact_version_list match it holds the advisory's bound past the version (its fix, or the versions just above its last affected or listed version), so it may start above the version; where higher is advisory, the CNA's range that ends below it, the CNA saying the version is fixed), from an entry the record writes, or, with cna_range_default true, a span no entry writes that the record's defaultStatus covers. higher: the source the answer follows, the more conservative one (cna or advisory). note: the API's sentence on the dispute and what the answer does with it, relayed verbatim. Fields and values a later API adds are relayed. Its absence is not a finding that the CNA agrees: an API that does not serve it yet, or older than the field, sends none; one that serves it reads a CNA's ranges only where it applies them and only from an entry it matches to the package; and a match the CNA's range alone raises may carry none.

interval.description: The affected range holding the version (fixed is exclusive, last_affected inclusive): the advisory's, or, where version_evidence is cna_affected_range, the CVE record's CNA range; absent when none holds it.

verdict.description: affected (a range on record holds the version), not_affected (no range on record holds it), undetermined (a range could not be decided at it) or not_assessed (no advisory record, and no CNA package URL, names the package for this CVE; or only the CVE record's CNA names it, by package URL, and does not call this version affected, which alone never clears it; or the lookup did not run).

version_evidence.description: Registry match: how the version was decided: exact_version_list (named in the advisory's list of affected versions), advisory_interval (inside one of its intervals), fix_boundary_only (below its only stored fix, its lower bound assumed), no_version_supplied (no version given, so no claim about it), or, once EchelonGraph's API serves it, cna_affected_range (held by the CVE record's CNA range, where no advisory statement holds it: interval is the CNA's range, and fixed_in_dispute, where the API publishes one, says how the two differ; such a match may carry none; on a match whose match_method is cna package url, no advisory record names the package for the CVE at all, and the CNA's statement is the only source). Relayed as the API sends it; a later value is relayed too.

installed.description: The installed version asked for, as the API read it from the request headers, and its verdict against this CVE; absent when none was asked.

state.description: assessed, or not_assessed for a CVE record rejected by its numbering authority.

kind.description: The vendor's own category: vendor_fix, workaround, mitigation, no_fix_planned, none_available or other. One exception: a Cisco vendor_fix is no_fix_planned when the advisory's Summary says, in wording EchelonGraph's parser reads, that Cisco will not release a fix, and none of its Summary, Fixed Software, Recommendations, Details or Affected Products notes says, by the parser's markers, that a fix exists; its source_category then stays vendor_fix, its source_subcategory names the note its text is from, and it carries no url. Wording the parser does not read leaves the item vendor_fix, so a Cisco vendor_fix is not a finding that a fix was released.

product_ids.description: The vendor's own product identifiers the item applies to, the first 16.

source_category.description: The vendor's own name for the category (CSAF vendor_fix, MSRC Vendor Fix, Palo Alto work_around).

source_subcategory.description: MSRC's SubType, e.g. Security Update; for a Cisco no_fix_planned item, the title of the note its text is from (Summary); null elsewhere.

text.description: The vendor's text, verbatim but for HTML markup removed, cut at coverage.item_text_cap characters (text_truncated). Empty, with text_chars 0, when its advisory's vendor_text_withheld is true.

text_chars.description: The length of the vendor's text in characters.

remediation_state.description: parsed; none_in_source (parsed, and the advisory lists no remediation for this CVE, which is not a finding that no fix exists); not_parsed (EchelonGraph does not read this vendor's remediation, or has not yet read this advisory); withdrawn (the vendor rescinded it).

vendor.description: The vendor's slug. Each vendor's advisory data stays under its own licence, and EchelonGraph's terms add no restriction to it: redhat, Red Hat's security advisories, © Red Hat, Inc., licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; source https://access.redhat.com/security/data); github, the GitHub Advisory Database, licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; source https://github.com/github/advisory-database); microsoft, Microsoft's own terms (its advisory pages are not copied: the facts and EchelonGraph's title are served, with a link to Microsoft's advisory where it names a CVE ID); every other vendor, that vendor's own terms.

vendor_text_withheld.description: true: the vendor's remediation text is not served (Microsoft's): each item's text is empty; its kind, source_category, url, fixed_build and product_ids are served.

data_truncated.description: false: data is the answer whole. true: the structured result would pass 30,000 characters of JSON with data whole, so data is cut (DATA CUT): the entries of some of its lists keep only some of their fields, or the lists only some of their entries, truncated gives each, and no string is shortened. The same call with full: true returns data whole.

freshness.description: The producing radar's last completed check (last_run_at), where the API serves one.

measured_at.description: When the underlying observation was made, as the API states it; null when the answer does not say or holds no observation.

state.description: measured: a measurement of what was asked; an exposure count is measured only with measured_at and method. not_assessed: the answer holds no dated measurement of what was asked, so no count in it is presented as one; it can still relay a count, as what the source holds on record, undated, and its notes (and exposure_state, where the result carries it) say what each count is.

truncated.description: Present when data_truncated is true: each list of data that was cut, by its path in data (a dot between the names of an object and a list inside it), with total, its entries in the answer, returned, the entries data holds, and thinned, true when each of them keeps only some of its fields.

installed_asked.description: The installed version this call sent (in request headers), as given; null when none.

parsed_vendors.description: The vendors whose remediation EchelonGraph parses.

sections_failed.description: The sections the API could not read (its failed_sections); null when the answer does not say.

vendors_not_parsed.description: The vendors in this answer whose remediation EchelonGraph does not parse.

kind.description: What failed: the request (network, timeout), the answer (http, not_json, not_object, unexpected_shape), the input, or this server.

message.description: The cause: the API's own message, or what went wrong.

path.description: The API path requested, when a request was made.

status.description: The HTTP status, when the API answered one; 503 with kind internal and path null where this server was too busy to make the call.

state.description: failed: the lookup did not complete. invalid_input: the input was refused, so nothing was looked up. Neither is a finding.
